chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
The divorce of the slave girl is her sale, or the sale of her husband.

And he (peace be upon him) said regarding the man who marries his slave girl to a free man, then sells her: He (the free husband) is separated from her, unless the buyer wishes to leave them (to remain married).
ai.seo_question: How is the divorce of a female slave legally determined in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the mechanism of *talaq* (divorce) for slave women, establishing that their marital bond is severed upon sale (*bay'*) rather than through the formal declaration used for free women. It further clarifies the status of a free man married to a slave girl: if she is sold, the marriage dissolves automatically unless the new owner explicitly chooses to retain the couple together, reflecting the distinct legal status of slaves in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A'ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘A divorce of the slave girl is her sale, or sale of her husband’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said regarding the man who married his slave girl to a free man, then sold her. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is a separation of what is between them unless the buyer so desires to leave them (to be upon their marriage)’.
